issues.body: `value_key` accepts arbitrary `&str` predicate and graph values, then passes them to the existing `info` encoder, which performs `u16::try_from(p.len()).expect("context field < 64 KiB")`. Unlike the pre-existing callers whose context fields are fixed-size IDs, these new fields are caller-controlled RDF terms. Consequently `value_key`, `seal_literal`, `open_literal`, and `equality_tag` can abort the process instead of returning a fail-closed error when given a sufficiently long IRI. This is both a public-API correctness defect and a denial-of-service risk for clients operating on untrusted RDF.
issues.fix_hint: Make the new variable-length derivation path total: either encode context lengths with a sufficiently wide fixed-width length (and update/pin the golden vectors), or make key derivation return `Result` and reject oversized fields with `Error::LimitExceeded`. Propagate that result through `seal_literal`, `open_literal`, and (with an API update) `equality_tag`. Add a test using predicate and graph strings beyond the supported bound that verifies rejection without panic.
issues.title: Public value-key derivation panics on predicate or graph strings over 65535 bytes

verdict.summary: The Profile SE implementation and its disclosure posture are generally careful, but the new public key-derivation path can panic on caller-controlled RDF terms. This violates the fail-closed contract and creates a denial-of-service path in any client processing an oversized predicate or graph IRI. The tests cover ordinary and malformed ciphertext inputs but do not exercise this load-bearing input boundary.
